open_obligations: Check whether debate and market-making use the same number of turns.
Note that the supervisor is a model, not a non-expert human as in sandwiching.
Check that the four tasks have a strong-weak gap large enough for a sandwiching analogy.
out.other_title: Do debate, market-making and recursive reward modeling work in sandwiching trials?
out.rationale: Bowman et al. ask for empirical trials of debate and market-making. Lang, Huang and Li report that debate used in their approach performs better than all other variants, including market-making and consultancy, in test accuracy and PGR across all four tasks, at least in their settings; the 'weak supervisor' is a model, not a human.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate and market-making differ as sources of information for a weak supervisor, across the four tasks Lang, Huang and Li test

text: The paper reports that debate, as used in its approach, gives better test accuracy and PGR than all other variants, including consultancy and market-making, on all four tasks, and the authors note that consultancy is a relatively weak baseline because there is a 50-50 chance of the consultant arguing for the incorrect answer.
title: Debate beats consultancy and market-making on test accuracy and PGR across four tasks
